extracted.intended_audience: entry-level grant writers; nonprofit organizations; new academic faculty; foundation grant seekers
extracted.subtask_description: A general, entry-level guide to drafting a competitive grant proposal for foundations, government programs, or other funders, covering planning, narrative sections, budget, supporting documents, and submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funder alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify funders aligned with your project and explicitly connect the proposal to the funder's priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match the funder's language and priorities exactly; reference the funder's funded portfolio where relevant. Failure to align with the funder's priorities is a common reason for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to RFP/RFA requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the Request for Proposals (RFP) or Request for Applications (RFA) carefully and follow all stated requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note deadlines, page limits, formatting requirements, submission instructions, and required attachments. Match format requirements exactly; format violations can disqualify a proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication with program officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact the funder's program officer when you have questions about fit or application requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use program officer conversations to clarify priorities, eligibility, and expectations. Proper communication can improve alignment and reduce unforced errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear statement of need
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the problem clearly and document it with data to show urgency and magnitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite credible sources, quantify the problem and impact, and explain why intervention is needed now. Vague problem statements are a common fatal flaw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goals and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Articulate clear goals and specific, measurable objectives that the project will achieve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate high-level goals from concrete objectives (preferably SMART). Tie objectives to measurable outcomes used in the evaluation plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected outcomes and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify expected outcomes and the broader impact of the project on the target population or field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State short- and long-term outcomes and quantify them where possible. Include a sustainability plan if continued impact beyond the grant period is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology / project approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the methodology or approach showing how goals and objectives will be achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a realistic, research- or evidence-based methodology; explain steps, activities, and rationale. Unrealistic or vague methods weaken competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline and milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a timeline with milestones that shows when major activities and deliverables will occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear milestones and a schedule demonstrating feasibility. Timelines should align with the budget and personnel availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel, roles, and qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe project personnel, their roles, and relevant expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include CVs or biosketches for key staff; show that personnel match project needs. A personnel mismatch is listed as a common mistake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget completeness and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a detailed budget listing personnel, direct costs, and indirect costs (if allowed), and justify each line item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break out salaries/benefits, supplies, equipment, travel, and overhead; provide a narrative justification explaining why each cost is necessary and reasonable. Unrealistic budgets or poor justifications are frequent reasons for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation plan and metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a plan describing how the project’s success will be measured, with specific metrics and data collection methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify measurable indicators, data sources, collection methods, analysis plans, and reporting timelines. Lack of an evaluation plan or vague metrics is a common mistake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting documents and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide required supporting documents such as letters of support, IRB/IACUC approvals, organizational documents, CVs/biosketches, and references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all required attachments are present and tailored (e.g., strong, specific letters of support rather than generic ones). Missing required documents or generic letters weaken applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter content
rubrics_metrics.description: Write a brief cover letter introducing the organization/PI, stating the need, summarizing the project, indicating the amount requested, and giving contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep it concise and professional; use it to emphasize fit and provide a quick hook for reviewers or program officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive summary / project summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a one-page overview summarizing the problem, solution, impact, budget, timeline, and organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write this last (it’s often read first). Keep it concise and compelling—clear problem, proposed solution, and key outcomes. Make sure it mirrors language used elsewhere in the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and concision in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use plain language, avoid jargon, write in active voice, and structure paragraphs with topic sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define necessary technical terms; use bullet points where appropriate. Poor writing (vague wording, passive constructions, or excessive jargon) reduces persuasiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional presentation and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure error-free, consistent formatting with page numbers, headings, and appropriate white space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the funder’s formatting rules precisely; remove typos and inconsistencies. A professional-looking submission signals competence and care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-based approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Ground your proposal in credible data and research to justify the need and chosen methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite reputable sources, use data to quantify needs and expected impact, and show that your methods are research-informed. Unsupported claims or lack of evidence are weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision, review, and timely submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare multiple drafts, solicit outside reader feedback, conduct a final format check, and submit before the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow time for internal review and external feedback to catch logical gaps and errors. Late submission is an avoidable reason for failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of letters of support
rubrics_metrics.description: Include letters of support that are specific, demonstrate commitment, and clarify partners’ roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid generic or templated letters; strong letters describe concrete contributions, resources, or partnerships. Generic letters are listed as a common mistake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and regulatory approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Include proof of required ethical or regulatory approvals (e.g., IRB, IACUC) when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide documentation or timelines for approvals. Missing or incomplete compliance documentation can block award or delay funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how project activities or benefits will continue after the grant period, where relevant (especially for nonprofit grants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe plans for continued funding, organizational adoption, or scaling. Lack of a sustainability plan is cited as a common weakness.
